etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Middle French canal, from Old French canal, from Latin canālis (“channel; canal”), from canālis (“canal”), from canna (“reed, cane”), from Ancient Greek κάννα (kánna, “reed”), from Akkadian 𒄀 (qanû, “reed”), from Sumerian 𒄀𒈾 (gi.na). Doublet of channel.

definitions.definition: An artificial waterway or artificially improved river used for travel, shipping, or irrigation.
(anatomy) A tubular channel within the body.
(astronomy) One of the faint, hazy markings resembling straight lines on early telescopic images of the surface of Mars; see Martian canals
To dig an artificial waterway in or to (a place), especially for drainage

quote.text: In the mangrove-type salt marsh, the entire marsh must be canaled or impounded.

definitions.definition: To travel along a canal by boat

quote.citation: 1905, William Yoast Morgan, A Journey of a Jayhawker, page 211:
quote.text: Near Rotterdam we canalled by Delfthaven.
